statement: Under prediction, the corrected resampled t of Nadeau & Bengio as Bouckaert & Frank apply it to r repeats of K folds — t = mean(d)/√((1/(rK) + n₂/n₁)·s²_d) on rK − 1 df over the paired fold differences of the primary score — gives an approximately valid 95% interval and test for the difference between two families' cross-validated scores (and a family's and its baseline's) when computed on a repeated k-fold substrate of at least 10 repeats of K folds (default 10 × 5) drawn whatever validation leads; the K(K−1)/2 pairwise intervals are descriptive, uncorrected for multiplicity, because the choice is corrected by BBC-CV.
regime: Prediction; any task; folds not time-ordered; units kept whole; substrate ≥ 10 × K
decision: Pairwise family-difference sentences ('not distinguishable on these rows' / 'X is ahead on these rows') and the baseline verdict's interval
user_sees: "Ridge against Linear: log loss differs by 0.012 (95% interval of the difference −0.004 to 0.028; corrected repeated k-fold t 1.52 on 49 df, 10 × 5 folds): not distinguishable on these rows."
claimed_basis: Nadeau & Bengio, Mach Learn 2003;52:239; Bouckaert & Frank, PAKDD 2004; folds.COMPARISON_REPEATS comment 'Bouckaert & Frank 2004: 10 × 10'; COMPARISONS_NOTE (validation.py:581).
notes: [part id F2-003] test_ms6_prediction_validation.py::test_2_the_corrected_repeated_kfold_t_matches_a_numpy_hand_computation checks the formula only, not coverage. Code-vs-source: Bouckaert & Frank recommend 10 × 10-fold; the app's default is 10 × 5 (COMPARISON_REPEATS=10, K=5). Nadeau–Bengio's correction was derived for random subsampling with a heuristic correlation; its coverage on repeated k-fold is approximate. Overlap: folds.py COMPARISON_REPEATS (F1), validation.py contract 'comparison_substrate' (:893) and its 'at least 10 × K' stated text.

statement: The random forest's standard settings — 500 trees, each on a bootstrap of every row, mtry floor(√p) for classes and max(floor(p/3),1) for a number, smallest leaf 10 rows for class probabilities and 5 for a number — are randomForest's/ranger's defaults (a true random forest, unlike scikit-learn's regressor default max_features=1.0, which is bagging), and using 10 as a minimum leaf rather than ranger's minimum node size is a stricter but acceptable departure.
regime: prediction; random_forest; every size (standard candidate; kept alone below n_plan 300)
user_sees: Describe: "500 trees, each on a bootstrap draw of the rows; each split tries the square root of the number of columns, and every leaf holds at least 10 rows; the trees' class shares are averaged into probabilities." Quiet term "randomForest's and ranger's defaults".
claimed_basis: Liaw & Wiener 2002 (randomForest); Wright & Ziegler 2017 (ranger); Probst, Wright & Boulesteix 2019; RECIPES §2.2.
notes: [part id F4-008] The test compares against the R packages' documentation strings (independent reference for provenance). Constants at forest.py:65-66, :271-273, settings :370-390, describe :407-415. The 'stricter but acceptable' part (leaf vs node size) has no test.

statement: Under Estimate or Describe, relabeling a two-valued covariate or energy column that is not the exposure, the outcome, a declared modifier or the fixed-effects column (coding its two spellings the other way round, with no blank and no third spelling) leaves the exposure's coefficient, its interval and the fitted values exactly unchanged and only flips the sign of that column's own coefficient, so the finding's repair changes no reported number and needs no calibration or post-lock check.
regime: Estimate or Describe purpose; finding whose repair family declares reparameterizes and whose offered options only relabel; every affected column has role covariate or energy and is named by no other answer; any outcome type or model family the primary uses
decision: Triage disposition of an open data finding at the gate (open-noticings sweep)
user_sees: Recommended "Doesn't change your numbers here": "Coding `gender` the other way round only flips the sign of its own coefficient; the estimate for `sugar`, its interval and the fitted values stay exactly as they are."
claimed_basis: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell (Frisch & Waugh 1933; Lovell 1963), named in materiality_calibration.json 'invariance' entry; SURFACING_POLICY §2.6 as amended; WAVE_C6A_PLAN §7 ruling 2 (orchestrator, 2026-10-10)
notes: [part id F6-001] Also sweep.py:519-546 (recommend rule 2), sweep.py:484-506 (adjustment_only), materiality.py:219-225 (invariance), materiality.py:1086-1092 (verify: not graded). The existing test checks OLS with classical SEs only. FWL is an OLS theorem; for logistic, Cox, GEE or mixed models the invariance follows from MLE equivariance under reparameterization (the citation is then a misnomer, though the conclusion should hold given an intercept or baseline hazard). Referee should confirm it also holds for the intervals actually reported (HC3, cluster-robust, survey Taylor linearization, MI-pooled) and for any penalized shrunk table, and that the model always carries an intercept.

statement: The within-strata residual with total energy kept in the outcome model has the standard model's estimand: its nutrient coefficient is the standard model's exactly, because the residual and total energy span the same model as the nutrient and total energy.
regime: residual method with strata (e.g. within sex) and total energy kept
decision: estimand sentence and row meanings shown for the stratified residual
user_sees: The standard model's substitution, with the nutrient in its own units: the residual and total energy span the same model as the nutrient and total energy, so the coefficient is the standard model's …
claimed_basis: none specific to strata (inherits McCullough & Byrd 2023 from the pooled residual)
notes: Implicit: StratifiedEnergyAdjuster.estimand() returns METHOD_TABLE['residual'] (energy.py:1392-1396); describe_model gives form 'residual' whatever the strata (energy.py:1597-1602, 1703-1704) and swap rows 'total energy fixed' (1757, 1815); stages/modeling.py:702 adds no strata wording. With level-specific slopes b_s and level constants, N_adj = N − Σ_s 1[s]·b_s·E + level constants, which lies in the span of (N, E, C) only if every b_s is equal and the strata indicators are covariates. test_wp3::test_1_the_null_holds_with_sex_in_the_model_too uses y ~ within-sex residual + energy + age + sex as its reference, not the standard model.

statement: Under inference, losing more than 10% of the rows to complete-case analysis is enough to warrant a concern, shown with a comparison of the kept and dropped rows' outcome and predictors.
regime: inference; complete-case strategy; share of rows dropped > 0.10
decision: concern on the fit (complete-case row loss)
user_sees: Complete cases drop N of M rows (x%), more than the 10% at which CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK flags listwise deletion. ... multiple imputation keeps every row.
claimed_basis: CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK anti-pattern 1 ('Flag when listwise deletion drops >10% of rows')
notes: ROW_LOSS_SHARE at missing.py:87. test_wp7::test_7_* check the threshold and the pooled-SD SMD arithmetic only. The kept-vs-dropped comparison can only reveal dependence on observed variables.

statement: The distribution of single-day 24-hour recall intakes, or of each person's mean of two recalls, is wider than the distribution of usual (long-run average) intake, so percentiles and the share below a cut-off read from it are wrong in both tails; the NCI measurement-error model is needed and the mean-of-days distribution is ranked lower and shown only beside it, labeled.
regime: inference purpose, dietary lens; a nutrient or food with repeated 24-h recalls on at least a subset (>=2 people with >=2 recalls)
user_sees: Option 'The distribution of each person's mean of recalls' labeled "unsound for percentiles and prevalence: the tails are too fat; shown only beside the usual-intake distribution, labeled"
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §03 ('Averaging 2 days leaves too much within-person variance in the distribution; the tails are too fat'); Tooze et al. 2006, 2010
notes: Also methods/usual_intake.py:3-8. The test is on a known-truth simulation.

statement: With repeated pairs per person, the SD of a single difference combines between- and within-person variance components from a one-way ANOVA (σ²_b = (MS_b - MS_w)/λ, truncated at zero, λ = (n² - Σm_i²)/((k-1)n)), the bias's variance is (σ²_b·Σm_i² + σ²_w·n)/n² on t(k-1) (or the person-means variance over k when σ²_b is truncated), and the limits' intervals come from Zou's MOVER.
regime: Describe or Predict; persons with more than one pair; not under a survey design
user_sees: "Each of the N people contributed several pairs, so the SD of a difference combined the between- and within-person variance components (Bland & Altman 2007), with MOVER confidence intervals for the l…
claimed_basis: Bland & Altman 2007 (J Biopharm Stat 17:571); Zou 2013 (Stat Methods Med Res 22:630)
notes: Docstring :36-49. Unbalanced case: test_unbalanced_repeated_pairs_are_bland_and_altman_2007s_anova; truncation: test_a_truncated_between_person_variance_takes_zous_standard_error_for_the_bias. Applying MOVER to unbalanced data is the app's extension.

statement: For a continuous outcome a held-out score needs at least 100 held-out rows, and for a multiclass or ordinal outcome at least 100 held-out rows in the rarest class or level, to be useful, so below that cross-validation alone is offered first.
regime: continuous, multiclass or ordinal outcome; a 20% holdout below the floor
decision: Order of the split question's options
user_sees: "A convention: at least 100 held-out rows, by analogy with the 100-event rule for binary outcomes."
claimed_basis: Labeled a convention by analogy with the binary 100-event rule; no citation.
notes: The app itself flags these as conventions (convention=True). | Overlaps F2-018 (row_previews.py:637 holdout floor of 100), merged into F1-016. | Inventory source id: F1-017.

statement: A column holding a single value carries no variation any model can use, so it is settled as excluded without asking.
claimed_basis: "a constant has no variation for any model to use" (KIND_RULES role:excluded, readings.py:1172).
notes: Low-risk; included for completeness. 'Single value' is among non-missing rows: a column that is constant where observed but missing elsewhere may carry information through its missingness. | Merged duplicates: F2-023 at turbotab/core/stages/rows.py:591. | Inventory source id: F3-017.

statement: For NHANES data the correct survey weight is the weight of the smallest subsample on which all analysis variables were measured (the least common denominator): an OGTT analyte requires the OGTT subsample weight (WTSOG*), a fasting analyte (glucose, triglycerides, LDL, insulin, apoB) the fasting subsample weight (WTSAF*), dietary recall variables the day-1 dietary weight (WTDRD1*, or the two-day WTDR2D* when day-2 variables are present), and otherwise the MEC examination weight; a variable recorded only where a subsample weight is positive (at most 1% of its rows outside, missing on at least 5% of the table, at least 10 rows) is that subsample's variable whatever its name; that weight is offered first, then the weights of the samples that contain it.
regime: NHANES (2-year, pooled multi-cycle, 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic) tables with weights and design columns.
decision: Which survey weight is offered first (Recommended) for design-based estimates.
user_sees: Survey question with the least-common-denominator weight first and the variables that set it ("because"), or "needs `WTSAF2YR`" when the table lacks it.
claimed_basis: NHANES Tutorials, Weighting Module: "You must use the weight of the smallest subpopulation that includes all the variables you want to include in your analysis."; "A good rule of thumb is to use 'the least common denominator'..."; CDC codebook names (recognizers.py:1773-1812). SUBSAMPLE_SLACK/MIN_MISSING/MIN_ROWS are "TurboTab's own tolerance".
notes: rank_weights recognizers.py:1846; subsample_variables :1888; WEIGHT_TIERS :1798; FASTING_ANALYTES :1813. When unknown or unconfirmed subsample weights exist, 'settled' is False and the choice is the user's. test_wp13_recognizers.py::test_6/test_6b and test_recognition_leash.py::test_a4 check behavior against the rule, not the rule. | Merged duplicates: CW-015 at turbotab/core/survey.py:235 (offered); turbotab/core/stages/finding_words.py:626 (source: 'the least common denominator'), :707 (_survey_weights). | Inventory source id: F3-039.

statement: Batch entered as a covariate must enter as categories (one indicator per batch), so a numeric-coded batch column must first be confirmed as a code and the column settled as a covariate before the answer is accepted.
regime: batch method 'covariate'; batch column numeric/integer dtype or role not settled
user_sees: Refusal batch_covariate_unsettled: "As a covariate, `batch` enters the outcome model as categories, one indicator per batch. Confirm that first."
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14.2 (readings confirmed before they change a number).
notes: Pinned by test_ms7_omics::test_5c. | Inventory source id: F5-039.

statement: For internal validation at typical clinical sample sizes, bootstrap optimism correction is the recommended default, repeated cross-validation is acceptable, and a single train/test split is the weakest option.
decision: the validation scheme's order on the seal card
user_sees: Bootstrap optimism correction is the recommended default and repeated cross-validation is acceptable; a single train and test split is the weakest option at typical clinical sample sizes.
notes: 'Typical clinical sample sizes' undefined. The app itself does not apply the bootstrap to boosted trees or forests (D-022), and BEATS_PREDICT §17.2 recommends a single sealed latest period under Predict; the seal card offers 10–30% holdouts.

statement: Under a population survey design, a subgroup analysis keeps every row and marks the domain, since deleting rows drops PSUs and strata from the variance and gives wrong standard errors; variances are Taylor-linearized with first-stage units sampled with replacement and t intervals on the PSUs minus the strata holding the domain's rows.
regime: survey design with weights, strata and PSUs; exclusions or complete cases under the population answer
user_sees: To restrict to a subgroup, keep every row and mark the subgroup ... Deleting rows drops PSUs and strata from the variance and gives wrong standard errors.
notes: Also voice.py:897-904 and 2408-2413; term content.py:785-786. Deleting rows does not always change the SEs materially; the df rule is NCHS's convention.

statement: Internal–external cross-validation across survey cycles is summarized by random-effects meta-analysis of the log MSE with a Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman interval and a prediction interval for a new cycle on t(k − 2), because on the identity scale cycles with larger MSE have larger standard errors and so less weight, which is optimistic.
user_sees: for a new cycle, 24.4 to 42.0 (95% prediction interval)
claimed_basis: Riley et al. 2016; Higgins, Thompson & Spiegelhalter 2009; IntHout et al. 2014; Snell et al. 2018
notes: With k = 8 cycles τ² is imprecise. The engine serves the identity scale today (P27).
